# Concept based Ambiguity Resolution in LLMs

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#concept-ambiguity-resolution)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-10**

[Original source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v328/main/assets/hu26b/hu26b.pdf) · CPAL 2026 proceedings, PMLR 328:940–956; publisher-linked 17-page PDF, titled Concept based Ambiguity Resolution in LLMs.

**Reading coverage:** All 17 PDF pages: Sections 1–5, references and Appendices A–E; all equations, Algorithm 1, Table 1 and Figures 1–11 with captions/examples. Figure-dependent entropy, detection, API-retrieval and distance-pattern results on PDF pages 5, 9, 10, 14 and 15 were visually inspected.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Published metadata](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v328/hu26b.html) · [Associated preprint record (title differs; first submitted 16 May 2025, current record v3 dated 1 October 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11679) · [Coauthor institutional publication record](https://research.unsw.edu.au/people/dr-liming-zhu/publications?type=conferencepapers)

## Research question

Models may repeatedly produce one reading of an ambiguous request, leaving ordinary embedding similarity or sampled agreement insensitive to alternative interpretations.

## Method

Few-shot examples encourage two interpretations. Sparse-autoencoder features supply masked concept representations for an approximate path-kernel distance, using straight-line interpolation from zero to final weights rather than the original training path. A separate supervised concept predictor retrieves API calls.

## Evaluation

Ambiguity detection uses AMBROSIA questions and generated interpretations treated as unambiguous controls. Distances are compared with dense embeddings; the classification threshold is the intersection of the plotted class-density curves. A 20-question activation study and a separate Gorilla TensorFlow Hub retrieval experiment provide supporting evidence.

## What the results support

The paper reports 86.25% detection accuracy versus 70% and 77.75% for dense-distance baselines in this constructed comparison. Targeted activation improves aggregate self-judgment but decreases ambiguous-class accuracy. The best concept-retrieval variant slightly exceeds the compared fine-tuned Gorilla API-call result, while domain accuracy remains lower.

## Limits and qualifications

A held-out threshold-selection protocol, independent validation of generated negative labels and repeated-run uncertainty are not clearly reported. Internal activations and model-specific SAEs are required. Limited activation examples support a mechanism hypothesis, not a universal explanation of ambiguity. No SQL execution, active clarification, refusal or user-outcome evaluation is provided.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Directly relevant to pre-generation ambiguity detection for database questions; its API-retrieval result should remain separate from claims about SQL generation or resolving a user’s intended interpretation.
